header.name: Multicore Parallel Programming and Runtime Systems
header.description: Computing hardware is becoming increasingly complex and is constrained by power and energy limits. As a result, contemporary platforms rely on multicore processors that scale to over one hundred cores, feature wide vector units, maintain complex memory hierarchies, and often share memory with accelerators such as GPUs. Conventional thread-based programming models impose significant complexity in organizing code into multiple threads of control and balancing work to ensure efficient resource utilization. These limitations have driven the development of parallel runtime systems that assist programmers by efficiently scheduling parallel tasks across available compute resources. This course introduces the fundamentals of parallel programming on multicore processors and explores the design and implementation of low-overhead runtime systems that manage task scheduling and resource allocation to improve performance and energy efficiency.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to explain the fundamentals of parallel programming and the different programming models widely supported in industry for multicore processors

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to design and implement a low-overhead load-balancing runtime for a task-based parallel programming model

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to implement runtime solutions to improve the performance of parallel applications on modern multiprocessor servers

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to develop an understanding of and assess runtime techniques that improve the energy efficiency of parallel applications on multicore processors

lecture_topics: shared memory parallel programming using POSIX Thread APIs
Introduction to task-based parallel programming models
greedy scheduling using work-sharing and work-stealing
programming models and runtimes for improving locality on a NUMA machine
Sequential overheads in dynamic load balancing
runtime techniques to dynamically control task granularity and minimize deque overheads
runtime techniques for detecting and avoiding false sharing
Achieving energy efficiency in parallel programming using runtime techniques, such as DVFS, and dynamic concurrency throttling
introduction to GPU computing using Boost.Compute
applying maching learning techniques in parallel runtimes
